chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar said: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban said, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Auramah, that Yahya ibn Yahya said on the authority of Abd Allah ibn al-Samit, on the authority of Abd al-A'la, from the Servant of God Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said:

Verily, Allah - there is no god but He - is Ever-living without quality or place, and He was not in anything, nor on anything. He did not create for His Position any space, nor was He strengthened after creating things. Nothing that comes into being is like Him. He was not devoid of power over dominion before creating them, nor will He be devoid of power after they cease. He, the Mighty and High, is a God who is Ever-living without accidental life, a King before creating anything and a Master after creating it. Allah has no limit, and is not known by anything that resembles Him. He does not age due to permanence, nor does He become stunned by the call of anything; and by His Fear all things become stunned. Allah is Ever-living without accidental life or described existence, without limited quality or fixed place or stationary location, but He is Ever-living by Himself, and the Master who has always possessed power. He created what He willed when He willed, by His Will and Power. He is the First without quality, and will be the Last without place. Everything is perishable except His Face. His is the creation and the command; blessed is the Lord of the worlds.
ai.seo_question: What are the attributes of Allah's essence regarding life, space, and quality according to Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from Musa ibn Ja'far (AS) elaborates on the divine attributes of essence, emphasizing that Allah is Ever-living without accidental life, quality, or place. It asserts His transcendence over space and time, His eternal power, and His uniqueness, concluding with the Quranic affirmation that everything perishes except His Face. Within the Shia tradition, this narration is pivotal for establishing *tanzih* (transcendence) against anthropomorphism, specifically clarifying that God's existence is not contingent on 'how' (*kayf*) or 'where' (*ayn*), distinguishing His eternal essence from created beings.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 6. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-`Attar said: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban said, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Auramah that Yahya ibn Yahya said on the authority of `Abd Allah ibn al-Samit, on the authority of `Abd al-A`la that Al-`Abd al-Salih Musa ibn Ja`far (AS) said:

Verily, Allah, there is no god but He, is Ever-living, but not in terms of quality or place. He is not in thing or on anything. He has not created for His Position any space. He is not strengthened through creation. Nothing that he has created is like Him. He was not powerless over things before their creation, not will He be powerless over them after they have gone. He, the Mighty and High, is the Ever-Living god without accidental existence. He is the Sovereign before creating something and He is its Master after creating it. Allah does not have any limits. He is not recognized by a thing that may be His like. He is not subject to aging. He does not raise His Voice to invoke anything, and with His Fear all things become stunned. Allah is Ever-Living, and not the product of accidental existence or a depicted existence. He neither has a restricted quality, nor a still space, but He is Ever-Living by Himself and the Master who is Eternally Omnipotent. He created what He willed when He willed, with His Will and Power. He is the First without any quality, and the Last without any space. Everything is perishable but He (His face). His is the creation and the command; blessed is the Lord of the worlds.
